frontMatter.about:
Established in 1988, Hikal is a reliable partner to companies in the Pharmaceutical, Animal Health,
Biotech, Crop Protection and Speciality Chemical industries. We manufacture and supply quality Active Ingredients, Intermediates, Biocides to the global life sciences industry.
Hikal has five manufacturing facilities in India at Maharashtra (Taloja and Mahad), Gujarat (Panoli) and Karnataka (Jigani and Bengaluru) and a world-class Research & Technology centre at Maharashtra (Pune). Our facilities have been inspected and certified by the respective Global Regulatory Authorities. We create and deliver sustainable solutions for our partners and customers across the life-sciences
value chain.
Motto
Just the right chemistry
Mission
To create value through superior, chemical products and operate as a responsible company.
Building trust and respect of our customers, shareholders and employees using science, technology and sustainable processes in harmony with the environment.
Vision
To be the leading global fine chemical company to the Pharmaceutical, Crop Protection and Speciality Chemical Industries.
We at Hikal
Have pledged to embrace our Core Values and Culture Pillars.
At Hikal, every challenge is met with:
“Why Not ”
Hikal is the partner of choice for:
- Pharmaceuticals (Human & Animal Health) Active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), generics, custom manufacturing, intermediates and advanced intermediates
- Crop Protection & Speciality Chemicals Active ingredients, advanced intermediates, intermediates, biocides
- Research & Technology
Process development, new product development, contract and custom development
Hikal is one of the first Indian companies to receive the Responsible Care® certification granted by the International Council of Chemical Associations (ICCA).

chapters.title: Code of Conduct
chapters.text:
Purpose
To establish a common understanding of the standards of behavior expected of all Hikalites (employees) at work or otherwise throughout their association with the company
Scope
- Applicable to all Hikalites (employees) and consultants, including Directors of the Company as well as people engaged on contract across sites
- Applicable to the vendors and suppliers associated with Hikal
Basis of the Code of Conduct Policy
Being a Hikalite
Every employee shall be proud to be a Hikalite. Being a Hikalite means:
Employee’s Responsibilities
- To get familiarized with this code of conduct available with respective HR and on Hikal Compass (intranet)
- To respect the company’s values and ensure compliance with the code of conduct, all policies and procedures at all times
- To report any violation or breach of any principles set forth in this code of conduct knowingly or unknowingly, directly or indirectly
Conflict of Interest
- Each employee is expected to avoid situations in which his or her financial or other personal interests or dealings are, or maybe, in conflict with the interests of the company; A conflict of interest occurs when one’s private interests interfere in any way, or even appear to interfere, with the interests of the company
- Hikal expects its employees to act in the company’s interest at all times; Employees are advised not to engage in any other business, commercial or investment activity that may be in conflict with their ability to perform their duties and responsibilities to the company; Employees must not use company’s assets, properties, information or position or opportunities arising from these for personal gain
Potential Conflicts (not limited to)
- Contracting business activities partly or wholly to any business entity managed by a close friend and or family member, directly or indirectly, unless authorised by Hikal management in writing
- Acting as a consultant, director or officer to a supplier,
customer and / or competitor of Hikal
- Significant ownership interest: Being invested in companies which have or seek to have business relationship with Hikal or which act as competitors of Hikal; If such investment is made before accepting employment at Hikal, the same shall be disclosed in
writing at the time of the interview or before accepting the offer of employment at Hikal
- Hikal respects potential contractual obligations of its employees with their former employers and refrains from creating any conflict of interests hence, any person joining Hikal shall declare all relevant information at the time of interview or accepting the offer or before joining Hikal
Concurrent Employment
Hikal employee shall not, without the prior written approval of the Chairman & Managing Director or Joint Managing Director & CEO of the company, accept employment or a
position of responsibility (such as a consultant or a director) with any other company, nor provide “freelance” services to anyone; In the case of Chairman & Managing Director/ Joint Managing Director & CEO, such prior approval must be obtained from the board of directors of the company
Protecting Company Property
The assets of Hikal shall not be misused; they shall be employed primarily and judiciously for the purpose of conducting the business for which they are duly
authorized; It is every employee’s responsibility to safeguard and properly use company assets and resources, as well
as assets of other organizations that have been entrusted to the company; These include tangible assets such as
IT assets, equipment and machinery, systems, facilities, materials and resources, as well as intangible assets such as information technology and systems, proprietary information, intellectual property, and relationships with customers and suppliers
Integrity of Data Furnished
Every employee of Hikal shall ensure, at all times, the integrity of data or information furnished to the company
Protecting Intellectual Property
- Valuable intellectual property includes patents, trademarks, logo, copyrights, products, technology and trade secrets; Our employees have a responsibility to protect these assets; Written approval shall be taken from corporate communications department for usage of company’s logo or any other classified information
by any employee
- Employees should only disclose confidential information on a need-to-know basis subject to management approval and a non-disclosure or confidentiality agreement and to take measures to avoid unauthorized disclosure, e.g. by securing access to confidential company records

chapters.title: Leave
chapters.text:
General Rules and Guidelines
- This policy is applicable for all employees, probationer
and trainees of Hikal
- Temporary employees or consultant are not governed by this policy
- Technician / workman shall be governed by agreed LTS at respective sites
Definitions & Entitlements per Year
Privilege Leave - 30 days
This leave is provisioned to facilitate employees to go on vacation from time to time to take rest or rejuvenate & spend exclusive time with family & get back to work recharged
Leave meant for enabling employees for unseen or unplanned personal exigencies
Sick Leave - 7 days
As the name suggests it’s meant to be availed on account of sickness
Maternity Leave - 26 weeks
Meant for female employees for taking proper care of herself during pregnancy and post childbirth
Paternity Leave - 5 days
Meant for male employees for the maximum of two children
Adoption Leave - 15 days
Employees are eligible for Adoption Leave to adopt a child. Legal agreements documenting the adoption must be produced
Accounting Year of Leave
Accounting year of all types of leaves shall be from 1st January to 31st December of the calendar year
- Privilege Leave: All employees are entitled to privilege leave from their DOJ on a pro-rata basis (2.5 days for each completed month)
o An employee is recommended to avail at least 5 days PL during the year and balance PL unutilized as on 31st December can be carried forward
- Leave Travel Assistance (LTA):
o LTA will be payable only when an employee actually proceeds on leave for a minimum period of 5 working days sanctioned in advance as per the leave policy in force else LTA can be claimed subject to tax
- Leaves for Trainees: All the trainees such as Management Trainee (MT’s), Graduate Engineer Trainee (GET’s),
Post Graduate Trainee (PGT’s), Graduate Trainee (GT’s), Diploma Trainee (DT’s) and Technical Trainee are eligible to avail 10 (Ten) days of leave
- Procedure for Applying Leave:
- All planned leave must be discussed with reporting manager and once in agreement, leave application must be completed through LMS in emPOWER
- In case of urgency, if leave like CL or SL is taken, the same must be regularized within 2 days of resuming work
- Intervening holidays or weekly off will not be treated as leave
- Cancellation of Leave: The department head can cancel the sanctioned leave in case of work exigency
o If an employee proceeds to avail the cancelled leave then those days will be treated as absence from duty and the rules pertaining to absence from duty will be applied
- Extension of Leave: As it is necessary to get prior approval for leave, so it is also necessary for extension of leave
- The employee has to apply to his/her department head for extension of leave well in advance and get it sanctioned to avail them
- In case an employee overstays, the unsanctioned leave will be treated as absence from duty
- Absence from Duty: When an employee takes off from duty without prior leave approval or proper intimation under certain unavoidable circumstances, then those day/days will be treated as absence from duty
- The days of absence will be treated under Leave without Pay

arrangement for employees travelling on official duty to company’s manufacturing sites, R&D Centers, Hikal offices, customer visits, or other business purposes etc.
Guiding Principles
- Lowest Cost to Hikal/Planet
Where there are reasonable options which have a materially different impact on ultimate cost, we will collectively work to minimize the cost to Hikal,
and environment
- Presumption of Trust
In all expense related matters, we assume that staff will behave prudently and ethically; Falsification of receipts and fraudulent claims will result in possible disciplinary action and employee termination
- Good Judgement at all Times
Actual expenses incurred and submitted for reimbursement must be business related and add value to the company
Expenses raised for personal benefit, including but not

visits for sightseeing / personal reasons, accompanying family members, entertainment etc., are the responsibility of the individual incurring the expense and should not be submitted for reimbursement
If in doubt, raise the issue with the Manager or Finance before expenses are incurred

## Parigyaan – Rewards & Recognition Policy
“Parigyaan” meaning recognition, is a Reward and Recognition policy at Hikal, which aims at creating a culture of recognizing accomplishments, extra-ordinary efforts and achievements of all employees
Objective
- Recognize and promote positive behavior of the employees for achievement of the business objectives
- Increase employee productivity and adherence to all compliance & quality systems
- Foster the culture of innovation using the philosophy of “Why Not?”
All employees on the rolls of the company shall be covered under “Parigyaan”
Categories of Rewards & Recognition:
At Company Level
- Chairman’s Excellence Award
- Individual Excellence Award
- Team Excellence Award
- Best Manufacturing Site Award
- Long Service Award
At Site Level
- Employee of the Month
- Spark Award
- Spot Award
Local Level Awards
- Site specific recognition other than the above-mentioned award categories, can be worked out in consultation with the Head HR
## Employee Referral Scheme
Objective
To leverage employee’s network to identify right talent through references of existing employees and also to provide employees with an opportunity to refer competent professionals for recruitment in Hikal
The Process
All vacant POSITIONS will be advertised internally at respective site by Site HR Head.
- Employee who wishes to refer someone against the advertised position can send the CV to respective HR along with ER Form
- All referred CVs will be evaluated by HR against the Job Description of the position
- Short listed CVs will be sent to hiring manager for technical evaluation
- If short listed by hiring / functional manager, HR will inform the employee in writing about the short list along with an appreciation letter and a pen recognizing the efforts put in by the employee
- HR will inform the referring employee about the date of interview and the status of interview
- If the person is selected and joins the company, the referring employee will be rewarded as per the program payout mentioned below
- The first payout to the referring employee will be done on successful completion of probation period of the referred candidate
- As to make the referral program more robust and quality driven, one more payout will be made to the referring employee on successful completion of 1st appraisal (one full year) of the referred candidate by attaining a rating between 4 & 5
- The referring employee must be there on the rolls of the company at the time of confirmation & completion of the 1st appraisal of the referred candidate
- If the referring employee resigns after sending a person’s cv and is serving the notice period at the time of confirmation of the referred candidate, he / she will not be entitled for the payout

chapters.title: Performance Management System (PMS) in emPOWER
chapters.text:
Purpose
Performance Management System at Hikal is a process of establishing high performance work culture and a
shared understanding about going beyond organizational objectives. It’s about aligning organizational objectives with individuals’ key result areas (KRAs). The emphasis is also on improvement, learning and development to achieve the overall business strategy and to create and sustain
high-performance work culture & ensure everyone contributes positively to business objectives. emPOWER in Oracle Fusion is fully online system, which facilitates PMS.
Features of PMS at Hikal
- Ensures alignment of the employee KRAs with the Corporate Measures
- The KRAs are cascaded down from the Corporate Measures, to the Management Committee members, Operations Heads, Functional Heads, Department Heads to every team member
- Facilitates set appropriate key performance indicators as a yardstick for measuring performance
- Monitors, measures and reviews performance periodically
- Facilitates improved performance in the areas identified
- Ensures that poor performance is addressed, and employee productivity is enhanced through performance improvement plan (PIP)
- It’s an online consistent, equitable and fair system meant for every employee
- Promotes joint responsibility and accountability between the managers and team members on performance management processes by inculcating a culture of on-going performance monitoring and feedback
Components of PMS
There are 2 key components of PMS – Defining KRAs and Performance Appraisal & Review. Both the steps are supported by constant sharing of feedback and learning inputs with the employees.
Components of PMS
Performance
Stage II: Performance Appraisal & Review
At Hikal, we follow a 3 stage Performance Appraisal & Review Process which is as follows:
- A. Self-appraisal by the employee
- B. Appraisal by immediate senior
- C. Review by the reviewer
General Guidelines
- At each stage of appraisal, the appraisee/appraiser and the reviewer should check the following in the system:
- Score for KRA & competency
- Training needs
- Specific remarks
- Drop down selection - Performance Review - Dialogue completed - YES/NO
- The overall rating will carry a weightage of 80% for KRAs and 20% weightage for competencies
- At each KRA / competency, the achievement score should be mentioned
- This score reflects the % achieved in the specific area
- The justification for each rating must be mentioned at
all the 3 levels i.e. appraisee, appraiser and reviewer
- Overall rating, scores and performance descriptors for reference:
[table]
| Rating | Descriptor |
| 5 | Significantly exceeds expectations |
| 4 | Exceeds expectations |
| 3 | Meets expectations |
| 2 | Doesn’t meet expectations |
| 1 | Poor |
- In case of Appraisees whose ratings are 2 & below, both the appraiser and the reviewer should give feedback
to the Appraisee and counsel him/her to improve the performance within a specified time period of 6 months; They should identify the key areas of improvement and chart an action plan
- The Appraisals should be conducted in a fair and un-biased manner to create a healthy performance driven environment; The Appraisals should not be
biased with respect to religion, region, gender, personal relationship, informal feedback, department, section or
